en.title: Minimum Total Cost of Repeatedly Merging Two Numbers
en.description:
Each time, choose two elements at different positions, pay their sum, and replace the two elements with that sum. Continue until only one element remains, and find the minimum total cost.

This site independently compiled the standard I/O and solution; bounds missing from the source and corrections to the examples are stated explicitly in the protocol.
en.input: The first line contains n, and the second line contains n integers. Full original bounds: 2≤n≤10000, 0≤a[i]≤100000. The answer may exceed the range of a 32-bit integer.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 28; 9; 9. They were verified by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Use a min-heap: each time, take out the two smallest numbers and merge them, add the merged value to the total, and put it back into the heap.
